extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive evaluation benchmark for multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains, systematically evaluating capabilities across instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis.
extraction.creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang
extraction.publisher: Peking University, Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence, Fudan University, University of Science and Technology Beijing, Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics
extraction.citeAs: Luo et al., RoboBench: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models as Embodied Brain, arXiv:2510.17801, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from large-scale real-world robotic datasets and in-house collections. The process involved curating datasets across diverse embodiments, attribute-rich objects, multi-view scenes, and memory-driven navigation. Specific workflows included preprocessing, annotation using VLMs (e.g., Gemini), detection models, or human experts, and Q&A format generation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Large-scale real robotic data from open-source datasets (e.g., Open X-Embodiment, RH20T, RoboMIND) and in-house collected robotic manipulation videos.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data was standardized into multiple-choice QA formats. For planning, frame sequences were extracted from videos and mapped into function templates. Explicit instructions were rewritten into implicit forms using LLMs. Quality control involved filtering for image quality and task validity, and removing items that all models solved correctly or failed to solve (with manual review for the latter).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: General and task-specific filters were applied during construction to address image quality and task validity. Sub-benchmarks had tailored rules, such as excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks. Data was standardized into multiple-choice QA formats for perception and instruction comprehension.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were created using a combination of automated tools and human experts. VLMs (specifically Gemini) were used to generate structured annotations like task summaries, step-wise instructions, and metadata. Human annotators refined these annotations. For failure analysis, execution-level failures were labeled by experts, while planning-level failures were synthesized by perturbing correct instructions. A majority-vote strategy was used for quality control.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A two-stage quality control process was adopted: data filtering during construction and post-construction validation. 20 professionally trained annotators conducted comprehensive quality inspections validating linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. A majority-vote strategy was employed to filter out trivial or impossible items.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Multiple (varies by dimension; includes multiple-choice, planning steps, point predictions)
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to advance robotic intelligence by systematically evaluating the cognitive capabilities of MLLMs. It highlights limitations in current models regarding implicit instruction comprehension, spatiotemporal reasoning, and failure diagnosis, guiding the development of more robust and generalizable embodied AI systems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset draws from large-scale real robotic data and in-house collections, covering diverse embodiments (single-arm, dual-arm, mobile), objects, and views. However, performance gaps exist between closed-source and open-source models, and between explicit and implicit instructions, indicating potential biases in model training data or evaluation metrics.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current models exhibit severe degradation on implicit instructions, fragile spatial-temporal perception, and difficulties with complex planning (dual-arm coordination, rare-object reasoning). Execution-level failure diagnosis is particularly challenging, with even human evaluators scoring lower than on planning tasks. The benchmark relies on simulated world models for planning evaluation, which may not fully capture all physical constraints.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) for embodied robotics. Specifically for evaluating instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis.
